states.partial: Applies conditionally or in a weaker form
states.no: Not the model this law uses

gdpr.note: Consent is one of six legal bases. When relied on, it must be affirmative.

ccpa.note: An opt-out model. Processing must be necessary and proportionate, and you can opt out of sale, sharing and sensitive uses.

lgpd.note: Consent is one of ten legal bases. When relied on, it must be prior and affirmative.

pipl.note: Consent is the primary basis and must be affirmative.

ukgdpr.note: Consent is one of seven legal bases. When relied on, it must be affirmative.

fadp.note: Processing by private persons is generally lawful without consent, subject to principles.

pdpa-ar.note: Prior, express, informed consent is the rule.

pipa-kr.note: Consent is one of several bases, but Korea relies on it heavily.

appi.note: Consent required for sensitive data and third-party sharing, not all use.

nzpa.note: Principle-based collection. No blanket opt-in requirement.

popia.note: Consent is one of several grounds. When relied on, it must be affirmative.

kdpa.note: Consent is one of several bases. When relied on, it must be affirmative.

dpdp.note: Clear affirmative consent required, with limited legitimate uses. From 13 May 2027.

pipeda.note: Consent is required, but implied consent can do for less sensitive information.

pa-au.note: Necessity-based collection. Consent is not the default gate.

pdpa-sg.note: Consent is required, but deemed and notification-based consent are allowed.

gdpr.note: Consent must cover each purpose, with separate choices where appropriate.

pipl.note: Separate consent for listed cases, such as sharing, sensitive data and transfers abroad. New purposes need fresh consent.

ukgdpr.note: Consent must cover each purpose, with separate choices where appropriate.

fadp.note: The purpose must be recognizable. Separate consent is not mandated.

lpdp-uy.note: Consent tied to the informed purpose.

pipa-kr.note: Separate consent required for each distinct purpose.

appi.note: Use limited to the notified purpose.

nzpa.note: Use limited to the purpose of collection.

popia.note: Processing tied to a specific, explicit purpose.

dpdp.note: Consent limited to the specified purpose, with an itemized notice. From 13 May 2027.

pipeda.note: Consent covers the purposes identified. A new purpose needs fresh consent.

pa-au.note: Use is tied to the purpose of collection, and consent must be specific.

pdpa-sg.note: Consent covers the purposes notified up front, with no rule on splitting them.

ccpa.note: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information rather than prior consent.

lgpd.note: Specific and highlighted consent for sensitive data.

pipl.note: Separate consent for sensitive personal information.

fadp.note: Consent must be explicit where it is relied on. It is not required just to process sensitive data.

pdpa-ar.note: Sensitive data needs a general-interest ground set by law, or anonymous research use. No one can be forced to give it.

lpdp-uy.note: Express written consent required for sensitive data.

appi.note: Prior consent required to acquire special care-required data.

nzpa.note: No special-category consent rule. The same principles apply.

popia.note: Special personal information requires consent or a listed exception.

kdpa.note: Needs a specific statutory ground, which does not include consent. Explicit consent is needed to send it abroad.

pipeda.note: Express consent is generally expected for sensitive information, not strictly required. Quebec requires it.

pa-au.note: Sensitive data needs consent, but consent can be implied.

pdpa-sg.note: No special consent rule for sensitive data.

fadp.note: No statutory withdrawal rule. In practice you object, and further processing then needs justification.

pdpa-ar.note: Consent can be revoked at any time, but no rule says withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.

lpdp-uy.note: Consent may be withdrawn, but no rule says it must be as easy as giving it.

pipa-kr.note: Consent may be withdrawn at any time.

popia.note: Consent can be withdrawn at any time, but no rule says withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.

kdpa.note: Consent may be withdrawn at any time, through a simple method. No rule says it must be as easy as giving it.

dpdp.note: Withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent. From 13 May 2027.

pipeda.note: Consent can be withdrawn at any time with reasonable notice.

pa-au.note: Regulator guidance says you can withdraw consent. The Act sets no procedure.

pdpa-sg.note: Withdraw any time on reasonable notice, and organizations cannot forbid it.

gdpr.note: A lawful-basis framework. Consent is one of six bases, and legitimate-interest processing runs until you object.

lgpd.note: A legal-basis framework. Legitimate-interest processing runs until you object.

ukgdpr.note: A lawful-basis framework. Consent is one of seven bases, and legitimate-interest processing runs until you object.

fadp.note: Closer to an opt-out posture. Processing is lawful unless objected to.

pipa-kr.note: Consent-based framework. The other bases are narrow.

appi.note: Third-party provision can use an opt-out filing.

nzpa.note: Principle-based. Neither strict opt-in nor opt-out.

popia.note: A justification-based framework. Legitimate-interest processing runs until you object.

kdpa.note: A lawful-basis framework. Legitimate-interest processing runs until you object.

pipeda.note: Implied, opt-out consent can work for non-sensitive information people would expect.

pa-au.note: Direct marketing works on opt-out. Other uses follow necessity rules.

pdpa-sg.note: Deemed consent by notification works as an opt-out. Not for marketing.

gdpr.note: For online services offered to children, parental consent below 16, or a lower national age of at least 13.

ccpa.note: Opt-in for sale or sharing of data of consumers under 16.

lgpd.note: Consent from a parent for children, in their best interest. Since 2026, the ECA Digital adds age checks and guardian-linked accounts.

pipl.note: Guardian consent for minors under 14, treated as sensitive.

ukgdpr.note: For online services offered to children, parental consent below 13. Ministers can now raise the age to as high as 16.

fadp.note: General principles apply. No fixed child-consent age.

pdpa-ar.note: AAIP guidance lets minors consent according to their maturity, with no fixed age.

lpdp-uy.note: No fixed age in the law. The regulator expects parental consent and weighs the child's maturity.

appi.note: PPC guidance expects guardian consent for children aged about 12 to 15 and under. A statutory under-16 rule is not yet in force.

popia.note: Processing children's data needs consent of a competent person.

kdpa.note: Consent of a parent or guardian for a child.

dpdp.note: Verifiable parental consent required for children under 18, from 13 May 2027.

pipeda.note: Guidance says children under 13 generally need a parent's consent. Quebec sets 14 by law.

pa-au.note: No set age. Organizations assess capacity case by case, or may presume it from age 15. A children's code is pending.

pdpa-sg.note: No rule in the law. Regulator guidance sets expectations for children's consent.
